summary: Intermittent candidate-id misassociation after proxy buffer rotation causing rerank order flips and elevated tail latency
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports intermittent rerank result order flips accompanied by 95th/99th percentile latency spikes (~400-1200ms) for rerank requests. The failures correlate with requests that include batched embedding payloads and HTTP/2 multiplexing across an edge Envoy proxy.

Impact: AtlasSearch saw degraded relevance (top-5 order changes) impacting search quality for ~2% of queries during peak and a 7% increase in tail latency. Affects enterprise production traffic in us-east and sporadically in eu-west.

Environment: Production, traffic through the managed edge (Envoy) -> api-gateway -> embed-ingest -> reranker path. Customer uses pinned model open-embed-v2 for embeddings and redwood-reranker-2.1 for reranking; requests originate from AtlasSearch's multi-tenant front end using HTTP/2 keepalive with request multiplexing.

Observed behavior: Some rerank responses return candidates with mismatched metadata (candidate ids that belong to a different query) or correct candidates but incorrect scores, and the request logs show additional queueing on the reranker pod that correlates with Envoy stream resets and buffer rotation events.

Expected behavior: Reranker returns scores for candidates submitted in the same envelope and preserves ID mapping and order. Latency should remain within SLA (p95 < 250ms).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use customer-supplied repro: batch size 16 embeddings with variable-length vectors (256-1024) and send over HTTP/2 multiplexed streams with concurrent 12 streams from a single client connection.
2) Route through edge Envoy configured with response-buffering and HTTP/2 stream multiplexing (customer and Redwood default configs).
3) Trigger sustained load for ~10 minutes at 120 qps and observe rerank order and tail latencies.
4) Compare candidate ids returned to the original request envelope; mismatch and order flips occur intermittently (~1-3% of requests in repro).

2026-03-10T14:22:11Z  WARN  api-gateway: incoming batch id=atlas-req-9832; assigned mux-tag=0x7f3a
2026-03-10T14:22:11Z  ERROR reranker[replica-3]: candidate-id mismatch detected; expected ids=[c1,c2,...] got ids=[c1,cX,...] correlation_id=atlas-req-9832
2026-03-10T14:22:12Z  INFO  ingest[proxy-shim]: http2 stream reset code=NO_ERROR stream_id=45 connection=10.2.3.14:43722
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: Envoy's response buffer rotation + HTTP/2 stream reuse resulted in ephemeral header/mux-tag recycling; the request envelope tag used by reranker for candidate mapping was overwritten or misattributed under high concurrency.

Confirmed correlation between Envoy buffer-rotation events and reranker queueing/p95 spikes using traces from TRACE_ID=trace-atlas-20260310-14-22. See span sequence: envoy->api-gateway->embed-ingest->reranker; a short-lived stream reset precedes the mismatch in ~78% of sampled failures.
Reproducer validated on staging by toggling HTTP/2 max-concurrent-streams from 100->25; incidence dropped from 2.3% -> 0.1% in 30m window. Suggests a concurrency-sensitive bug in mux/tag handling.

Found a race in the embed-ingest proxy-shim: when a stream reset occurs with pending chunks, the shim can reassign the internal envelope id to a new incoming stream before the reranker has consumed the pending batch. This leads to candidate metadata mapping to the wrong envelope in the reranker input buffer.
Related code pointers: proxy-shim request-id assignment (github/serving/pkg/proxy/shim.go line ~412), suspected race around ResetHandler and AssignEnvelope calls.
comments: 2026-03-10T15:03: Sarah (Support): Acknowledged. Escalating to SRE for priority investigation and providing a repro to Eng. SLA first response met.

2026-03-10T16:10: Liam O'Connor (SRE): Reproduced on staging with customer repro. Observed same Envoy buffer-rotation events. Creating a scoped jt for a fix and adding temporary mitigation flag to edge Envoy config to disable response buffering for affected routes.

2026-03-11T09:22: Maya Chen (Support): Customer confirmed improvement after mitigation; quality regressions dropped but still seeing rare occurrences under sustained load. Customer asks for ETA on permanent fix and whether any data integrity was lost.

2026-03-11T10:05: Liam O'Connor (SRE): No data was permanently lost; affected requests returned incorrect candidate mapping but logs show both versions; we'll roll forward a patch to ensure envelope ids are immutable once assigned and survive stream resets. Target patch in PR #1823.
resolution_notes: Workaround applied: disabled response buffering + reduced max-concurrent-streams on the edge Envoy for AtlasSearch route (rolled 2026-03-11 02:30 UTC). Observed reduction in incidence to <0.2% during 6h smoke test.

Fix in progress: code change to make envelope id assignment atomic and retained across stream lifecycles in proxy-shim. PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/1823. Patch includes unit tests that simulate stream reset race and an integration test in staging.
Planned rollout: staged deploy to prod canary (5% traffic) 2026-03-13; full rollout pending 24h canary metrics (p95 latency, mismatch-rate).

Follow-ups: add an automated alert for candidate-id mismatch rate >0.1% and update reranker ingest contract with stronger envelope immutability guarantees. Notify security/compliance that there was no exfiltration.
